'''Jeffery Lewis Tallon''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|CNZM|size=85%}} (born 1948) is a New Zealand physicist specialising in high-temperature superconductors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/funds/marsden/marsden20/jeff-tallon/ |title=Jeff Tallon |year=2012 |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=5 November 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141217113854/http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/funds/marsden/marsden20/jeff-tallon/ |archive-date=17 December 2014 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Tallon was born in [[Hamilton, New Zealand|Hamilton]] on 17 December 1948, the son of Phyllis Blanche Tallon (née Currie) and George Frederick Tallon.<ref name="HBTQ">{{cite book |last1=Taylor |first1=Alister |last2=Coddington |first2=Deborah |author-link1=Alister Taylor |author-link2=Deborah Coddington |title=Honoured by the Queen – New Zealand |year=1994 |publisher=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa |location=Auckland |isbn=0-908578-34-2 |page=358}}</ref><ref name="Whos who"/> He grew up in [[Mount Albert, New Zealand|Mount Albert]], and was educated at Gladstone Primary School, and later [[Mount Albert Grammar School]] in [[Auckland]] from 1962 to 1966.<ref name="Whos who"/><ref>{{cite journal |date=2010 |title=Congratulations |url=http://www.mags.school.nz/Folder?Action=View%20File&Folder_id=438&File=10-76-quarterly-T1-2010.pdf |journal=Mount Albert Grammar School Quarterly |volume=5 |issue=1 |page=18 |access-date=5 November 2014 |archive-date=4 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104133828/http://www.mags.school.nz/Folder?Action=View%20File&Folder_id=438&File=10-76-quarterly-T1-2010.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="ThenandNow">{{citeq|Q117189974|page=151}}</ref> After a [[BSc|BSc(Hons)]] at the [[University of Auckland]], he undertook doctoral studies at [[Victoria University of Wellington]] under Stuart Smedley and [[William Robinson (scientist)|Bill Robinson]], completing his PhD in chemistry in 1976.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.victoria.ac.nz/scps/about/attachments/ChemHist_second-edition_lowres.pdf |title=Chemistry at Victoria the Wellington University |last=Halton |first=Brian |author-link=Brian Halton |year=2014 |publisher=Victoria University of Wellington |access-date=5 November 2014 |page=148}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Tallon |first=Jeffery |year=1976 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=Premelting and the Machanisms of Melting in the Alkali Halides |publisher=Open Access Repository Victoria University of Wellington, Victoria University of Wellington |doi=10.26686/wgtn.16958908 |url=https://openaccess.wgtn.ac.nz/articles/thesis/Premelting_and_the_Machanisms_of_Melting_in_the_Alkali_Halides/16958908/1|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 1971, Tallon married Mary Elaine Turner, and the couple went on to have three children.<ref name="HBTQ"/><ref name="Whos who">{{cite journal |editor-last=Taylor |editor-first=Alister |editor-link=Alister Taylor |title=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa 2001 |journal=New Zealand Who's Who, Aotearoa |year=2001 |publisher=Alister Taylor Publishers |location=Auckland |issn=1172-9813 |page=852}}</ref>

==Academic career==
He was awarded a [[Doctor of Science]] by Victoria University of Wellington in 1996, on the basis of a selection of published papers.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Tallon |first=Jeffery Lewis |date=1996 |title=Selected publications of Jefferey Lewis Tallon: a thesis submitted to the Victoria University of Wellington in fulfilment of the requirements for the degree of Doctor of Science [in Chemistry] |publisher=[[Victoria University of Wellington]] |url=http://tewaharoa.victoria.ac.nz/primo_library/libweb/action/display.do;jsessionid=4DD09497679F67FDB7DEAB7F419F5CC3?tabs=requestTab |access-date=15 August 2015 }}{{Dead link|date=October 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
[[File:Jeff Tallon CNZM investiture.jpg|thumb|right|Investiture of Tallon as a [[Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]] by the governor-general, [[Anand Satyanand|Sir Anand Satyanand]], at [[Premier House]] on 2 September 2009]]
In 1990, Tallon was awarded the Mechaelis Medal for physics research.<ref name="Whos who"/> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1993,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/fellows-1919-present/s-u/ |title=The Academy: S–U |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=5 November 2014}}</ref> and in 1998 he won the society's [[Hector Medal]] jointly with [[Paul Callaghan]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/hector-medal/recipients/ |title=Hector Medal |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=5 November 2014}}</ref> In 2002, Tallon was awarded the [[Rutherford Medal (Royal Society of New Zealand)|Rutherford Medal]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/rutherford-medal/recipients/ |title=Rutherford Medal |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=5 November 2014}}</ref> the highest award in New Zealand science. In 2011 Tallon was awarded the [[Dan Walls]] Medal by the [[New Zealand Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NZIP Award Recipients – New Zealand Institute of Physics |url=https://nzip.org.nz/about-nzip/nzip-award-recipients/ |access-date=2023-03-16 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 1990, Tallon received the [[New Zealand 1990 Commemoration Medal]].<ref name="Whos who"/> In the [[2009 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|2009 Queen's Birthday Honours]], he was appointed a [[Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to science.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dpmc.govt.nz/publications/queens-birthday-honours-list-2009 |title=Queen's Birthday honours list 2009 |date=1 June 2010 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=16 January 2020}}</ref>
